intro.default: Hey {first_name}, glad we got this on the calendar. I'm going to walk through the proposal section by section — takes about 12 minutes — then I want your questions before we close out. Goal is that nothing is confusing before you make a decision. Sound good?
intro.training_note: Slow down. This call is not about selling anymore. They already said they were interested. Your only job is to remove doubt. Don't add pressure — remove friction.

executive_summary.label: Executive Summary
executive_summary.goal: Restate their pain in their words — prove you were listening
executive_summary.script: So here's how I framed this — based on our conversation, the two or three biggest gaps for {business_name} right now are [restate their exact words]. Everything in this proposal maps to one of those. Nothing in here is filler.
talking_points: Use their exact words. Not your interpretation — their words. This is the most important thing you can do in the first 60 seconds.
Name the 2-3 services you're proposing and which gap each one addresses specifically
60-90 seconds max — this is a summary, not a replay of the discovery call
executive_summary.training_note: If you parrot their own words back at them, they feel genuinely heard. Most people have never experienced that from a vendor. It's your biggest differentiator and it costs nothing.

scope_breakdown.label: Scope of Work
scope_breakdown.goal: Walk every deliverable to a pain point — no feature lists
scope_breakdown.script: Let me walk through exactly what's included. Every piece maps to something you told me. [Service 1] — this is for [their specific pain]. [Service 2] — this handles [their next pain]. Nothing in here is because I thought it sounded good.
talking_points: Map every line item to a pain they named. 'This is for the Google Maps problem you mentioned.'
Call out what's NOT included proactively. 'This doesn't include paid ads — that's a separate tier.'
Name the first thing they'll see go live and when. 'By end of week 2, you'll have X.'
scope_breakdown.training_note: Surprises after signing destroy client relationships. Call out everything upfront — what's in, what's not, when things happen. Contractors deal with contractors who overpromise and underdeliver every day. Be the exception.

pricing_section.label: Investment
pricing_section.goal: Anchor value before the number — always. Price before value = sticker shock.
pricing_section.script: Before I give you the number — you told me you're missing roughly [X jobs] a month in {city}. At your average ticket, that's [$ amount] a year. What I'm about to show you is a fraction of that. The monthly investment for everything we walked through is [price].
talking_points: Always say their revenue leak number before you give your price
Give the monthly number — not annual. Annual sounds bigger and makes it harder to say yes.
If they react to the number: 'What were you expecting?' Let them tell you their anchor.
Payment terms: monthly retainer, month-to-month unless they want the annual discount
pricing_section.training_note: The order of operations matters more than the actual number. Value first, then price. Every time.

timeline_milestones.label: Timeline
timeline_milestones.goal: Make the first 90 days feel real and tangible
timeline_milestones.script: Here's what the first 90 days look like. Days 1-14, we're in setup — you'll see [specific first deliverable] by end of week 2. Days 15-45, [second deliverable] goes live. From day 45 on, the work is fully live and compounding — I'll send you a report every month showing exactly what's happening and where you stand, no hiding the numbers.
talking_points: Day 1-14: onboarding + access + foundation build
Day 15-45: first deliverables live — name the specific thing
Day 46-90: first measurable result they can point to

Set the expectation honestly: 'Week 1 is setup, not results. This is a build that compounds over time — I'll never pretend it's instant. What I guarantee is the work gets done and you'll always see exactly where it stands.'
timeline_milestones.training_note: Most early cancellations happen because the client had the wrong timing expectation. Set it explicitly now. Month 1 is setup. Month 2 is first movement. Month 3 is proof. Anyone who cancels in month 1 was never given the right expectation.

guarantees.label: Guarantees & Terms
guarantees.goal: Make saying yes feel safe — lower perceived risk
guarantees.script: Few things I want to be upfront about. First — it's month-to-month. No long-term contract unless you want the annual discount. Second — if the month-one deliverables don't match what I've outlined here, that month is on me. Third — you get my direct number, {rep_phone}. You text me, I respond. No account manager.
talking_points: Lead with month-to-month — watch their body language change
Month-1 deliverable guarantee — if setup misses, first month is free
Direct access to owner — no account manager layer
Annual discount option — never a requirement
guarantees.training_note: Contractors hate being locked in. They've been burned by 12-month contracts for services that stopped delivering in month 2. Lead with month-to-month and the tension drops immediately.

close.label: Close
close.goal: Ask for the business directly — no hedging
close.script: That's the full picture. Any questions on anything we walked through? ... [Handle questions] ... Based on everything, I think this is a clear fit for where {business_name} is going. You want to start the setup this week?
talking_points: 'Want to start this week?' — direct, not pushy
If yes: send the agreement while still on the call. 'I'll send it right now — keep me on while you sign it. Takes 2 minutes.'
If revision: 'What specifically feels off?' Get one concrete thing to fix.
If delay: 'What needs to happen on your end before you feel comfortable?' Name the actual blocker.
close.training_note: Don't end the call without a concrete next step. They sign, they give you a specific objection to fix, or they give you a specific date to follow up. Vague endings — 'I'll think about it' — kill deals. Force the decision one way or the other.
